theme: Let everything that has breath praise the LORD, Amen
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 150 again, slowly and aloud. You first met it as trumpets in Revelation 8 to 11. Now read it as the last psalm of the Psalter, the last chapter of your journey, and a summary of what the whole Bible is for.
settingTheScene: This is the second time in this unit that we read Psalm 150, and we are glad to return to it. The first time, it prepared us for the trumpets of judgment, and the last time, it is a closing word: the whole Psalter, with all its tears and joys, ends in praise. The same is true of the Bible’s whole story. After every lament, every warning, and every war, the last word is “Hallelujah.” In Revelation, the word “Hallelujah” (which means “Praise the LORD”) appears in 19:1-6, the only place in the New Testament where it is found.
observation: “Praise the LORD! Praise God in his sanctuary” (v. 1).
“Praise him according to his excellent greatness!” (v. 2).
“Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!” (v. 6).
interpretation:
The whole book of Psalms is a conversation between God’s people and God. It contains songs of trust and complaint, history and prophecy, kings and exiles. Its structure follows a path. The first Psalm begins with the blessed man who delights in God’s law, and the book ends with the entire creation breathing praise. It begins with a person and ends with the cosmos. It begins with study and ends with song.

The five verses of the psalm are a final summary of all the praise of the Psalter. Praise is to be given in “his sanctuary” and in “his mighty heavens”; in the earthly place of worship and in the heavenly one. We praise him “for his mighty deeds,” a summary of what he has done in creation, the exodus, the covenant, the exile and return, and finally in Christ. We praise him “according to his excellent greatness,” because who he is exceeds anything we can say. The music is all the instruments of Israel’s worship. Whether we have a trained voice or a tin ear, we can join the praise. And then the invitation to everyone: “Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!” The Hebrew word for breath (neshamah) is the word used in Genesis 2:7, when God breathed into Adam the breath of life. Every breath is a gift, and every breath is an invitation to praise.

Now we read it as the end of a journey. For 900 days, we have traveled through the story of God, from creation to new creation. We have seen the creation, the fall, the call of Abraham, the exodus, the law, the kings, the exile, the return, the coming of Christ, the cross, the resurrection, the birth of the church, the letters to the churches, and the vision of the end. In all of it, we have seen a God who keeps his covenant. The story ends not in despair but in praise. And the psalm that ends the Psalter is a template for the end of our lives: whatever our circumstances, we end in praise. And in Revelation 19, the multitude shouts “Hallelujah” four times. This is the sound of the new creation, and we can begin practicing it now.

“Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!” In the Hebrew, the last word of the Psalter is Hallelujah. Say it with the church of every age. Hallelujah.
connection: Genesis 2:7 mentions the breath of life. Psalm 1 is the opening of the Psalter. Psalm 145-149 are the other closing psalms of praise. Revelation 19:1-6 has the four Hallelujahs of the great multitude. Revelation 5:11-14 shows the whole creation praising. Ephesians 5:18-20 and Colossians 3:16-17 call for praise in the church. Hebrews 13:15 says to continually offer a sacrifice of praise. Philippians 2:10-11 sees every tongue confessing. Isaiah 43:21 says God formed his people to declare his praise. 1 Peter 2:9 says we are called to proclaim his excellencies. Romans 11:36 gives a doxology: from him and through him and to him are all things.
application:
Take a moment to look back at what God has done in your life over these years. Name three things that stand out, and thank him.

Sing or speak Psalm 150 aloud, and finish with a loud “Hallelujah.”

Let each breath today be a reminder that you were made to praise the LORD.
prayerPrompts: Praise the LORD in your own words, for his mighty deeds.
Thank him for what he has done over these days.
Let everything that has breath praise him.
